title: The Characterization of Intermittent Hypoxemia and Its Association with Sleep and Regulatory Behavior in Preterm Infants
summary:
Premature infants experience breathing difficulties more frequently than full-term infants. These difficulties sometimes manifest as brief episodes of oxygen desaturation, which are in some cases linked to abdominal contractions and resulting forced expiration. To date, little is known about how these breathing patterns develop or whether they are associated with subsequent problems regarding self-regulation. The aim of this study is, therefore, to investigate these breathing and behavioral patterns in premature infants in greater detail and to gain a better understanding of them.
For the study, premature infants will undergo examinations a total of three times—during their stay in the neonatal unit and following their discharge (twice while hospitalized and once during a follow-up appointment after discharge). These examinations involve sleep and respiratory measurements, during which parameters such as breathing rate, heart rate, and oxygen saturation levels are monitored. Additionally, video and audio recordings are made to facilitate a more precise analysis of the infants' movements and vocalizations. Parents will also complete questionnaires regarding their child's sleep, feeding, and self-regulation behaviors during the first few months of life. Ultimately, the insights gained from this study aim to contribute to improving the care and follow-up support provided to premature infants and their families.

interventions.name: The study is designed as a prospective, monocentric, longitudinal, interventional pilot study. It will enroll 30 preterm infants with a gestational age of ≤ 30 + 0 weeks. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Gestational age ≤ 30 0/7
Exclusion criteria:
Major congenital anomalies or inherited metabolic diseases or chromosomal anomalies that may have an adverse effect on breathing or ventilation; infants with primary palliative care, families without sufficient knowledge of the German language to provide informed consent and fill out a questionnaire.
